newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - May 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - May 19.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Prime Minister John Howard has raised the prospect of major tax reform in the Federal Government's second term and has hit back against increasing complaints from business that his Government lacks vision. Howard said fundamental changes to the tax syste will be required over the next five to 10 years. Page 1. --

Wallis inquiry committee member Bill Beerworth has criticised Australia's tax structure, claiming it prevents the country from becoming a world financial centre. The comments came after Wallis chairman Stan Wallis last week criticised the Government for acking vision and called for urgent tax reform.
Page 1. --

A report by management consultancy group Towers Perrin and International Market Assessment has suggested Australia's 'egalitarian ethos' helps to keep the pay of executives at a lower level compared to that of their American and European counterparts. Ths does however ensure the funds are shared more equally around the top levels of an organisation. Page 1. --

Manufacturing group Email Ltd has commenced common-law actions against unions involved in a lengthy strike which has closed its Melbourne subsidiary, Martin Bright Steels, for over six weeks. An application will be lodged today in the Victorian Supreme Court requiring unions and striking workers at the factory to lift their picket line. Page 3. --
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard has promised a fundamental reform of the tax system after the next election and says he will consider further labour market reform except the cutting of minimum wages. The Government has also indicated there could be two doubledissolution election triggers, the Wik issue and legislation to make small business exempt from unfair dismissal laws. Page 1. --

Drug baron George Savvas has been found dead in his prison cell only 13 hours after a plan to escape from Maitland jail with backpacker killer Ivan Milat was foiled by prison staff. Savvas told prison authorities last week he was a businessman, not a criminal, and had no place in jail. Page 1. --

Politicians are exempt from a Budget crackdown that makes workers wait five more years for their superannuation, despite claims by Prime Minister John Howard rules would "apply across the board". Members of Parliament who serve three terms or more will still receive their taxpayer-funded super many years before the new preservation age applying to the rest of the community.
Page 1. --

Blue Heelers actress Lisa McCune was awarded the Gold Logie for the most popular television personality at last night's Logie Awards. The Seven Network won the majority of the awards, overthrowing Channel Nine's usual dominance, by taking 11 of the 22 voted categories. Page 1. --
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Prime Minister John Howard has confirmed a major review of the tax reform system, including the consideration of a goods and services tax, will be on the Government's agenda if it is re-elected for a second term. Howard said a tax overhaul was inevitable and also indicated there may be further "evolutionary" changes to the industrial relations system. Page 1. --

The International Olympic Committee is expected to pressure Australian officials to lift the curfew at Sydney Airport for the period around the 2000 Olympics, and for more high quality hotel accommodation to be provided. The IOC is also expected to seek special Olympic traffic lanes between the Olympic village at Homebush and outlying Games venues. Page 1. --

Notorious prisoner George Savvas has hanged himself in his Maitland Prison cell. Savvas' "big disappointment" over a thwarted escape has been suggested by his jailers as the reason for his suicide. Savvas and three other violent prisoners had planned to overpower guards and then use makeshift ladders to scale the prison walls. Page 1.

A report by the National Health and Medical Research Council has recommended the morning-after pill be sold across the counter. Church groups have condemned the report, but it was welcomed by the Family Planning Association, with the report also recommening further testing of the abortion pill RU 486.
Page 1. --
THE AGE

Prime Minister John Howard gave a strong indication yesterday that tax reform would be on a second-term agenda if his Government was re-elected. Howard said he did not want to set a timetable for tax reform but there was no doubt that sooner, or later, te Australian taxation system would have to be reformed. Page A1. --

Victorian Government documents show the State Government has spent less than six percent of the Community Support Fund on services for problem gambling in the last 14 months. About 2000 people attended a rally yesterday to celebrate non-gambling related fun. Page A1. --

The Sisters of the Good Shepherd will become the third Roman Catholic order to investigate allegations of physical and emotional abuse at one of its children's homes in the 1950s and 1960s. The group said the claims, including those that young girls were locked up with dead bodies, were very distressing.
Page A1. --

Actress Lisa McCune, who plays Constable Doyle in the television series Blue Heelers, has won the Gold Logie for the most popular personality on Australian television. McCune also collected a Silver Logie for the most popular female actor. Page A1.
